title: Branding Increases Mental Switching Costs: Why You Keep Branding After Winning the Association
summary: Cody explains that when a customer won't buy within about 48 hours, your marketing goal is branding: owning an association in their mind. Continued branding raises mental switching costs by deepening the customer's emotional relationship with you, making it very hard for a competitor to uproot.

principles.text: If the customer won't buy within ~48 hours, your marketing goal is branding, not conversion.
principles.quote: If your customer won’t make a purchase within the next 48 hrs your marketing goal is branding.

principles.text: Branding means owning an idea or need in the customer's mind so they think of you the moment it arises.
principles.quote: What branding does is associate your company name with an idea.

principles.text: Clients usually underestimate how long their customers' purchase cycle really is.
principles.quote: One thing I’ve noticed with clients is that their estimation of a customer purchase cycle is less than what it should be.

principles.text: Mental switching costs exist alongside physical ones, because people form relationships with brands like they do with people.
principles.quote: But what’s often forgotten is that mental switching costs exist.

principles.text: Keep branding after you win the association; it deepens the relationship and raises mental switching costs.
Speak to customers regularly with what they want to hear, so your brand-idea association is hard to uproot.
principles.quote: But when we develop customer relationships, when we grow the level of affinity and speak to our customers more regularly with things they want to hear, we make it hard if not impossible to uproot the brand and idea association.
